reviews.text: We happened to pass by the shop, and it saddens me to see animals displayed like merchandise in shop windows. Animals are living beings, not consumer goods. Please inform yourselves about what you are supporting with such a purchase and what species-appropriate husbandry means.

I was extremely disappointed with the staff's service.

During my visit to the store, while looking at the animals, I had a very disappointing experience with a female staff member.

The staff member who assisted me was wearing a mask, had long pink nail polish and eyelash extensions, and gave a very stylish impression. At first, I thought she was a bright and approachable person.

However, her actual service was quite different.

There was a sign in the store that said "Staff don't speak English," so I used a translation app to communicate from the beginning. The staff member also told me to use a translation app, so I followed their instructions.

Initially, I was looking at a dog and tried to ask if I could touch it. However, the staff member refused, saying, "No, you cannot touch this dog."

Of course, I wasn't trying to ignore her instructions and touch the dog. I remained calm and was simply trying to understand why I couldn't touch it and what I should do.

Afterward, the staff member said something to the effect of, "I need to eat" and "I need to rest."

I thought, "Well, there's nothing I can do," and said, "Then, could another staff member help me?"

However, other customers were coming and going in the store at that point, and I thought, "If the staff member is on break, shouldn't another staff member be able to help?"

So I asked the staff member, "When will your break end?" but I didn't get a clear answer.

After that, I was repeatedly told "No" to touching the dog, and I tried to understand the reason while calmly explaining using a translation app.

And from what I saw before leaving the store, the staff member didn't seem to be on a full break, but rather walking around the store to check the situation.

Of course, I understand that staff members have the right to take breaks and need to eat.

What I found puzzling was why the option of "having another staff member help" wasn't available in that situation.

Furthermore, after that, foreign customers, especially Caucasian customers, came into the store. Meanwhile, I was repeatedly told "You can't touch the dog" and "We can't help you."

Therefore, I felt that because I am Asian, not Japanese, and a foreign customer, I was receiving different treatment than other customers.

Of course, this is just my own feeling at the time, and I don't intend to assume that the staff had such an intention.

However, at least to me, the treatment gave the impression of such a difference.

Furthermore, I was later informed that there would be an additional charge if I were to take the animal overseas.

I have absolutely no problem paying the necessary transportation and processing fees if I were to take the animal back to China.

Therefore, my question wasn't about the cost itself.

If I had told the staff I would pay all the necessary fees and still wanted to continue looking at other animals, how would they have handled the situation?

To me, the explanation regarding overseas transportation felt less like guidance on necessary procedures and more like an attempt to persuade me to stop looking at animals in the store and leave.

If there are official regulations regarding overseas transportation, I understand that. However, I would have liked those regulations to be clearly explained in a way that foreign customers could understand.

I have shopped in various countries, including the United States. I generally enjoy talking to people and I'm the type who likes to communicate happily with store staff.

That's why I was so surprised by the way I was treated this time.

Of course, it's not a problem that they can't speak English to foreign customers. I have no problem using translation apps.

However, when there are language or operational issues, I would have preferred them to work with me to find a solution rather than immediately refusing me.

I didn't become emotional or try to force myself to touch the dog. I was simply calmly asking questions.

Despite that, being repeatedly refused from the start made me feel very uncomfortable.

I don't mean to personally attack the staff.

However, I hope that in the future, they will provide more polite and easy-to-understand explanations and fair and flexible service to foreign customers.

The reason I asked to touch the dog was because I was considering buying it. Previously, a Japanese couple who clearly couldn't afford that dog played with it for over ten minutes, and the staff were very polite, but they ended up leaving the store without buying anything. That's the key point.
so sad to see how the animals are kept in small glass cages & treated like toys

As someone from Germany where there are quite strict animal welfare laws (and owning a dog myself) it’s incredibly sad to see something like that. Please do proper research before buying a puppy in such a store.
I highly recommend that people look up how pet stores source dogs before they purchase a dog here. Dogs at pet stores come from puppy mills and puppies are separated extremely early from their mom.

stopped by to see the animals. this puppy was violently chewing and pulling on a smaller puppies ear and tugging hard. we tried to tell the worker and she just shrugged it off and said “yeah they do that”. the puppy was legit screaming and i felt ill from it. a whole group of people gathered and was in shock that the workers let that happen, eventually so many people gathered and made a scene that the workers finally took the bad puppy out and slightly “scolded” it. after that they put the bad puppy back into the cage with the smaller, defenseless puppies. i was disgusted and angered deeply by this. the practices by this store are gross and i left feeling horrible. DO NOT SHOP HERE. they need to be out of business. poor puppies

Drawn in by the adorable puppies, we casually stopped by. As she gazed at a white Pomeranian, a female shop assistant named Ms. Kameno noticed and approached her, offering to let her hold the puppy. Having owned a dog myself and having visited numerous pet shops in search of one, I've developed an understanding of the staff's intentions. Ms. Kameno, however, never pressured us to buy. Instead, she spoke about the significant investment involved and emphasized that owning a pet isn't a once-in-a-lifetime purchase.

She also stressed the importance of trusting your initial intuition and compatibility, and shared her own experiences as a dog owner.

Furthermore, despite the puppy being very energetic, she taught us the proper way to hold it. When we followed her instructions, the puppy calmed down dramatically, and it even showed us a gentle expression. I've made many purchases in the past, and while the product itself is important, I've always believed that the personality of the staff is crucial. In the past, I've even bought a car I wasn't planning on buying because of the wonderful service I received from a dealer, and I've even recommended them to my family. Today, not only were the Pomeranians adorable, but Mr. Kameno's customer service was outstanding, and I seriously considered purchasing one.

My conclusion is that if I were to get a puppy, I'd like to raise it together with my partner from when it's a puppy, so I've decided to pass on it this time. However, once our circumstances are right, my partner and I would like to visit Mr. Kameno's shop together and purchase one.

I think if there were more staff like Mr. Kameno, the number of successful matches between puppies and people would increase even more.

Thank you so much for your wonderful service!
Disgusting way to see this type of merchant. Animals are not your commodities.

One of the dogs by the front window was thirsty and was trying to drink from a water dispenser that looked like it was made for hamsters, not dogs. The dispenser was completely empty, and the poor dog was desperately trying to get some water. It gave up and lay down. I went inside and told a staff member that the dog was thirsty. One of the staff members was busy with someone planning to buy a dog. She was so focused on making a sale that she didn't notice me standing behind her trying to tell the dog there was no water. I told another staff member who was passing by, but she just nodded and walked out of the store. I figured she wouldn't listen, so I told another staff member who was crouching behind the counter like a ninja. She gave me an OK sign and went on brushing another cat. If I were a staff member and a customer told me that, I would rush over and help the poor dog. In fact, I wouldn't want to work in a store this awful. It's the kind of place that sells ordinary white puppies at exorbitant prices to rich people who don't really love animals. Working, buying, or being associated with a store like this is shameful. Free the animals.

I bought a teacup poodle for 700,000 yen, but a year later it grew to the size of a regular toy poodle. I paid that price because I thought it was a teacup poodle and wouldn't grow big, so I think it's like fraud that it grew so much. Now I love my dog ​​and it's adorable, but I think this kind of practice is dirty. I wouldn't recommend buying a dog from here!
I find it unacceptable to put these animals behind glass. The sellers deserve to be where they belong.

Horrible place! How is this even legal? Animals aren’t toys and shouldn’t be put in glass boxes. It is such a horrendous shop that you shouldn’t support!! If you buy from this place, don’t fool yourself, you are just as bad as them exploiting animals.
